newsitem.title: NORWAY: Few oil firms to benefit from rising Norway output.
newsitem.headline: Few oil firms to benefit from rising Norway output.

text.p: Oil companies operating on the Norwegian continental shelf will have to search out news ways to shore up their short to medium-term crude production profiles, despite burgeoning output in Norwegian waters, industry analysts Wood Mackenzie said on Monday.

Wood Mackenzie said it had revised upwards forecasts for Norwegian crude and natural gas liquids (NGL) output in 1997 to 3.41 million barrels per day (bpd). The estimate is an increase of five percent, or 170,000 bpd, on the 1996 level of 3.24 million bpd.

But, it said, the increase was the lowest year-on-year rise in output in percentage terms since the 1980s and was significantly below increases of 12 and 14 percent achieved in 1996 and 1994 respectively.

"Moreover, the predicted increase iN output is being achieved by relatively few of the companies -- we forecast only 11 of the 26 companies currently producing oil in Norway will enjoy a year-on-year increase in output in 1997," a statement said.
Over the last year companies had benefited both from rising output and relatively high oil prices, which had boosted annual results.
"However, the widespread steady increase in equity production noew seems to be coming under presurre in Norway," the analysts said.
"As a result of this pressure, we anticipate an increase in corporate activity as the companies seek out ways to shore up their short to medium-term equity oil production profiles."
